thread:
IncidentBot: PAGER: high error rate in routing service — region edge-tier (us-west-2) spillover detected. page: oncall-nyc 
Janelle: on it, fetching dashboard and recent rollouts. seeing spike in 5xxs and increased latency in edge-tier queues. 
Ravi: flags — traffic to us-west-2 up ~3x for the last 7m, and fallback model selection started returning incompatible variants for a subset of requests. 
Marta: is this the canary from this morning? I rolled out a routing-policy tweak at 07:42 UTC that changed tiebreaker weights; could be related. 
Ken: joining. @Janelle handoff? 
Janelle: taking initial lead. mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) pin fallback model to gpt-compat-1 for edge-tier, 3) throttle cross-region spillover. executing now. 
Liam: notifying customers on affected plans — tier B and C are showing failures, ~48 unique customer API keys flagged. prepping status note. 
Janelle: paused routing-policy rollout: 
``` 
POST /admin/rollouts/stop
payload: {"policy_id":"policy-edge-tiebreak-v3","reason":"incident-2163021123"}
```
Ravi: pinned fallback model via admin: 
```
PATCH /models/pin
{ "model": "gpt-compat-1", "scope": "edge-tier" }
```
Marta: telemetry shows misroute cluster: requests with long prefix tokens were being sent to compatibility-tier, kernel mismatch produced 502s. snippet from logs: 
```
2026-02-21T07:53:41Z router[edge-3]: route_decision(policy=edge-tiebreak-v3) -> target=compatibility-tier-2
2026-02-21T07:53:41Z worker[compat-2]: decode_error: kv-cache-invalid for request id=xx7a9
2026-02-21T07:53:42Z response: 502 "model_incompatible"
```
Ken: hypothesis A: the tiebreak weight change exposed a mismatch between fallback model selector and model capability matrix. hypothesis B: autoscale for compat-tier lagged, causing queued timeouts -> perceived misroute. 
TelemetryBot: metric update — edge-tier 5xx rate: baseline 0.3% -> 12.6% at peak (07:51-07:56 UTC). queue latency (compat-tier) median 320ms -> 2.4s. 
Ravi: temporary mitigation in place: pinned model + paused rollout. early signs: 5xxs down to 3.1% after 90s. still seeing error tail. 
Janelle: rolling a guardrail: add a quick rule in router to prefer local-region pools for sessions with >64 tokens. applying: 
```
PUT /router/rules/quick
{ "if": "tokens>64", "prefer": "local-region" }
```
Marta: applied. checking logs for remaining misroutes. search query: 
```
index=router logs | where route != preferred_local and region==us-west-2 | stats count by target_pool
```
Ken: found 312 remaining misrouted requests, 68 of them hit compat-tier causing 502. others were queued out to warm-tier causing latency spikes but not errors. 
Liam: customer impact — we have 12 support tickets opened, a few customers logged automated retries and saw timeouts for async embeddings jobs; no broad data loss reported. drafting status update now. 
Janelle: handoff: I'm going to let Ken take on post-mitigation analysis while I coordinate comms with support/product. Ken, you have the triage. 
Ken: taking over. immediate next steps: collect correlated traces, gather kernel compatibility matrix, run replay on small sample traffic against pinned model. Ravi — can you drop the KV-cache dump for the error window? 
Ravi: uploading KV cache dumps and router traces to /shared/incidents/2163021123/logs. snippet: 
```
--- kv-cache-dump start ---
key: sess:abc123 kv_len: 12
... partial corrupt entries at offset 4096 .. 4128
--- end ---
```
Marta: timeline so far: 07:42 rollout (policy-edge-tiebreak-v3) -> 07:49 traffic surge to us-west-2 -> 07:51 fallbacks selected gpt-lite-3 for long prefix sessions -> 07:52 5xx spike -> 07:53 alert -> 07:54 pause rollout + pin fallback -> 07:56 initial drop in errors -> 08:01 guardrail rule applied -> 08:02 error tail decreasing. 
Ken: running replay with 1k sample requests now against gpt-compat-1 pinned config, checking for decode errors. will compare trace IDs against error log to validate hypothesis A. 
TelemetryBot: replay metrics: decode_error rate 0.9% on gpt-compat-1 (sample), vs 7.8% observed in live compat-tier during incident window. suggests autoscale/queue pressure contributed. 
Ravi: stack traces show worker OOMs in some compat instances at 07:50-07:52 — autoscaler scale-up delay ~45s. combined with incompatible model choice for long prefixes leads to the decay. 
Janelle: decide: root causes likely 1) rollout changed tiebreaker exposing long-prefix traffic to compat-tier, 2) fallback selector allowed gpt-lite-3 for those sessions (capability mismatch), 3) autoscaler lag increased queueing and timeouts. 
Marta: mitigation followups: add preflight capability check in routing decision for long-prefix requests; increase autoscaler aggressiveness threshold for compat-tier; add a canary test for routing-policy rollouts that simulates long-token sessions. 
Ken: collecting artifacts for RCA doc: router traces, kv-cache dump, autoscaler metrics, rollout diff, trace IDs. I'll tag them and start the timeline. 
Liam: status update posted to customers (incident-2163021123): short note + ETA for RCA. customers asked about retries; suggest guidance to implement exponential backoff during region fallback for large payloads. 
Janelle: thanks all. Ken — hand over to you for post-incident root-cause writeup. I'll close the pager in 30m if no regressions. :white_check_mark: 
Ken: acknowledged. creating internal RCA doc and will link in channel when ready. cc @Marta @Ravi for postmortem edits. 
IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged by Janelle, status: mitigated -> monitoring.
